newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed near flat levels on Wednesday after a quiet session and dealers said guilder bonds had to get somewhat cheaper before buyers would return to the market.
One dealer said he did quite some business in the 2003-area as a big buyer had shown interest in this segment.
"Business was thin, but surprisingly there was a big buyer for 2003-paper in the market and we also did some shortening business," said one dealer.
There was some selling of 30-year bonds against 2004-debt and ten-year paper was swapped against 2002-paper, he said.
Dealers said the Dutch yield curve was likely to steepen as the demand for long-dated bonds was fizzling out.
"The few buyers that are in the market go for short-dated debt," said one dealer.
They said the yield gap with Germany was likely to narrow further. The ten-year gap with Germany narrowed to minus 12 basis points from minus 13 on Tuesday.
"A range of minus 6 to minus 11 could be expected in the near-term," said one dealer.
